scope: A local HTTPS TestClient regression signs in a configured owner and two distinct invited recipients through a deterministic fake OIDC transport. Each denial request uses its own authenticated session and valid CSRF token where required.
private_browser_observation: The existing private HTTPS service loaded in Chrome. An incognito Google identity that is not the configured owner was rejected by the owner OIDC callback. In a separate regular Chrome profile, the configured owner authenticated and the owner workspace loaded; direct navigation to the review-state API returned a sign-in-required response, then the owner-state API still loaded under that owner session. This is one live authenticated owner-to-review read denial, not a complete bidirectional cross-role API acceptance.
limits: The automated role matrix uses fake OIDC transport and a local TestClient, not the installed private Linux service or live Google sessions.

The browser observation exercised only owner-to-review state read under a valid owner session. No live recipient-to-owner request, cross-recipient request or cross-role write was exercised; live authenticated cross-role acceptance remains open.

Two same-session access requests are created in the isolated local test before the no-mutation snapshot to establish valid CSRF and session authorization. The selected routes and recipients are regression coverage, not an exhaustive authorization audit.
No invitation, grant, run or model dispatch was created on the private service in this stage. Private-pilot readiness and owner acceptance remain open.
privacy: Contains no hostname, account, OAuth code, credential, invitation token, session cookie, transcript or private URL.
